purpose: Uncorrelated IN subquery (expected: unnested into a semi join)
sql:
SELECT c_custkey, c_name
FROM customer
WHERE c_custkey IN (SELECT o_custkey FROM orders WHERE o_totalprice > 500000)

extra.AI Reason: The optimizer uses a Hash Semi Join to efficiently filter customers based on the existence of orders meeting the price criteria.
Full scan of the customer table is efficient for retrieving all rows.
Build a hash table on the filtered orders to perform the semi-join.
Scan orders to find those matching the price condition.

differences.text: PostgreSQL runs part of the plan in parallel (Gather). The AI plan runs in a single process.
The largest disagreement on row estimates is at Nested Loop of (orders) with (customer): PostgreSQL estimates 150 rows, the AI 150,000 (factor 1000.0). Row estimates drive operator choice.

The join of (orders, customer): PostgreSQL uses Nested Loop of (orders) with (customer). The AI uses Hash Join of (customer) with (orders). Hash join suits large inputs. Nested loop suits a small outer input, especially with an index on the inner side. Merge join suits sorted inputs. The AI's reason: "The optimizer uses a Hash Semi Join to efficiently filter customers based on the existence of orders meeting the price criteria."
Join of (orders, customer): outer and inner inputs are swapped. PostgreSQL's outer input is (orders).
Join of (orders, customer): PostgreSQL performs an Inner join, the AI a Semi join.

Table customer: PostgreSQL uses Index Scan on customer using customer_pkey. The AI uses Seq Scan on customer. A sequential scan wins when many rows qualify. An index scan wins when few rows qualify. A bitmap scan sits in between. The AI's reason: "Full scan of the customer table is efficient for retrieving all rows."
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Aggregate (Hashed) over (orders) (computes aggregates (GROUP BY, SUM, COUNT, ...)).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Gather over (orders) (collects rows from parallel worker processes).
Only the AI plan has Hash over (orders) (builds the in-memory hash table for a Hash Join). The AI's reason: "Build a hash table on the filtered orders to perform the semi-join."

similarities: Both plans join the tables in the same order (every intermediate join result is the same).
Both plans use Seq Scan on orders.
